exposure: Mode of delivery (vaginal vs. caesarean section)
cohort: 63 pregnant women with abnormal cervical smears referred for pre-invasive lesions of the cervix at the General Hospital in Vienna, Austria between 2010 and 2015
finding: Mode of delivery did not significantly influence the natural history of cervical dysplastic lesions in pregnant women.
mod_finding: The number of spontaneous regressions to normal cervical cytology during pregnancy was similar between vaginal delivery and caesarean section.
